related_questions.question: What does COVID do to the brain?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 can affect the brain in various ways, including inflammation, neurological and psychiatric issues, and potentially long-term damage. Some individuals may experience encephalitis, leading to confusion, memory problems, and difficulty concentrating. Additionally, COVID-19 can trigger or exacerbate psychological disorders like depression, anxiety, or even psychosis. The virus can also impact the autonomic nervous system, affecting heart rate and blood pressure.

text_blocks.snippet: Long COVID, or post-COVID-19 condition, can involve a range of persistent health problems following a COVID-19 infection, even if the initial illness was mild or asymptomatic. These effects can manifest as ongoing symptoms like fatigue, shortness of breath, and cognitive difficulties, and can also lead to new diagnoses of conditions like heart disease, mood disorders, or autoimmune diseases.
snippet_highlighted_words: fatigue, shortness of breath, and cognitive difficulties

list.snippet: Fatigue: Persistent and debilitating tiredness.
Shortness of breath: Difficulty breathing, even with minimal exertion.
Cognitive dysfunction: "Brain fog," memory problems, and difficulty concentrating.
Sleep disturbances: Insomnia, difficulty falling asleep, or restless sleep.
Cardiovascular issues: Heart palpitations, chest pain, or irregular heartbeat.
Gastrointestinal problems: Digestive issues like diarrhea, constipation, or bloating.
Mood disorders: Anxiety, depression, and other mental health challenges.
Muscle and joint pain: Persistent aches and pains.

list.title: New diagnoses:
list.snippet: Long COVID can trigger the onset of conditions like heart disease, autoimmune diseases, lung disease, and kidney disease, according to the Mayo Clinic.

list.title: Worsening of pre-existing conditions:
list.snippet: Long COVID can exacerbate existing conditions like diabetes or hyperlipidemia.

list.title: Impact on work and quality of life:
list.snippet: Long COVID can affect the ability to work, leading to loss of productivity, income reduction, and reduced quality of life.

list.title: Potential for chronic conditions:
list.snippet: Some individuals may develop chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), or fibromyalgia, notes the CDC.
Not contagious: Long COVID is not spread from person to person.
Delayed onset: Symptoms can appear weeks or months after the initial infection.
Individual variability: The types and severity of long COVID symptoms vary widely among individuals.
Impact on work and productivity: Long COVID can significantly impact an individual's ability to work and maintain their quality of life, says the World Health Organization.
